threatModel.content:
# Threat Model

ph-vote is a self-hosted FastAPI application for browsing and rating video clips. A browser reaches static pages and JSON/media routes in app/api.py; app/guards.py enforces client-network and Host allowlists plus origin/fetch-metadata checks, while app/server.py composes file-backed store/index/media services. Runtime state is stored under configured data directories, and selected operations invoke yt-dlp/ffmpeg or contact adult-media sites and an optional more-like-this webhook. Docker publishes loopback by default and bind-mounts a host data directory (README.md:20-24, README.md:38-45, docker-compose.yml:6-30, app/api.py:91-159, app/server.py:58-89).

## Assets

- Integrity and privacy of votes, reasons, notes, highlights, skips, more-like-this requests, source metadata, scoreboard data, and download settings stored beneath DATA_DIR/SHARED_DIR/MEDIA_DIR/CACHE_DIR (app/config.py:64-70, app/store.py:12-25, app/store.py:238-268).
- Authenticated Pornhub session material referenced by PH_COOKIES_FILE and the upstream account authority it grants; the server may use it for one-tap favorites (app/config.py:94-101, app/clips.py:75-118).
- The optional MLT_WEBHOOK_KEY and webhook destination used to notify a separate digger service (app/config.py:81-89, app/store.py:499-513).
- Host filesystem confinement for downloaded media under DOWNLOAD_ROOT and integrity of files mounted into the container data volume (app/config.py:103-109, app/store.py:277-309, docker-compose.yml:10-14).
- Server and host availability while handling blocking upstream fetches, yt-dlp/ffmpeg work, media streaming, source scans, and concurrent HTTP requests (app/api.py:145-151, app/clips.py:577-630, app/clips.py:1184-1269).

## Trust Boundaries

- Browser or API client to FastAPI: every HTTP request is accepted only from ALLOWED_NETS and allowed Host names/ports; GET/HEAD under /api and /media receive cross-site checks, while JSON POSTs require same-origin fetch metadata or Origin and a bounded Content-Length. There is deliberately no login, so all clients admitted by this network boundary share application authority (README.md:169-174, app/api.py:91-136, app/api.py:543-566, app/guards.py:24-69).
- FastAPI mutation routes to local file-backed state: known clip identifiers and operation-specific validation precede atomic JSON writes; download directory settings are resolved with realpath beneath DOWNLOAD_ROOT (app/api.py:573-716, app/store.py:103-113, app/store.py:249-309).
- Configured source files and scout/digger outputs to the in-memory index and browser: app/index.py recursively scans SOURCES_DIR and reads JSON/HTML-derived metadata that later appears in JSON responses and DOM rendering; these files are trusted deployment inputs but remain a stored-content parsing boundary (app/config.py:64-70, app/index.py:3-149, app/api.py:249-378).
- Server to external media sites and CDNs: validated clip IDs select fixed site URL templates and media helpers invoke urllib, yt-dlp, and ffmpeg; the image proxy uses a hostname regex and phnet.py routes only configured adult-site suffixes through an optional proxy (app/sites.py:14-54, app/clips.py:326-430, app/clips.py:527-630, app/phnet.py:12-103).
- Server to privileged upstream capabilities: the favorite endpoint consumes a configured cookie file to mutate a Pornhub account, and the more-like-this flow may send a configured bearer-style key to a configured webhook. Any admitted browser client can request these operations because authorization is network-wide, not per user (app/api.py:610-641, app/clips.py:75-135, app/store.py:499-544).
- Deployment/operator boundary: Docker runs the application as a non-root user with /data mounted and publishes only 127.0.0.1 by default; scripts/ensure-up.sh is a separate operator-invoked recovery path that can manage Tailscale with passwordless sudo and is not reachable through HTTP routes (Dockerfile:28-40, docker-compose.yml:25-36, scripts/ensure-up.sh:68-176).

## Attacker Capabilities

- A network client inside an allowed CIDR who can send arbitrary HTTP paths, headers, JSON bodies up to the configured body limit, range requests, and repeated requests, but who does not initially control the server process, environment, local files, configured credentials, or operator account.
- A malicious website visited by an admitted user's browser that can attempt cross-site GETs or POSTs but cannot normally forge same-origin Origin, Sec-Fetch-Site, Host, or the client's source network; read_problem and write_problem are the expected controls (app/guards.py:43-69).
- A contributor or local automation process able to write configured SOURCES_DIR or shared scout/digger JSON can influence clip metadata and index inputs, but source access alone does not establish control of the HTTP host, credentials, or deployment environment.
- An operator who controls environment variables, .env, volume mappings, download roots, proxy destinations, or recovery scripts is already trusted with deployment authority; review seeks unintended privilege gain across these controls rather than treating authorized configuration as an attacker primitive.

## Security Objectives

- Only intended loopback, tailnet, LAN, or authenticated-reverse-proxy clients may read adult-content metadata or invoke state-changing, credentialed, download, and media-generation operations.
- Cross-site browser requests must not use an admitted user's network position to read private API/media responses or perform writes.
- Untrusted request fields and source metadata must not escape configured filesystem roots, become shell or subprocess code, create unsafe outbound destinations, or execute in the browser as active markup/script.
- Authenticated Pornhub cookies and webhook keys must remain server-side, avoid responses and logs, and be used only for their intended fixed upstream operations.
- Request, parsing, streaming, transcode, and background-job work must be bounded enough that an admitted client or malformed source file cannot trivially exhaust shared service resources.
- Atomic updates and concurrency controls must preserve file-backed data integrity across votes, highlights, downloads, skips, and more-like-this workflows.

## Assumptions

- The documented deployment is single-user/self-hosted and has no application login; the intended perimeter is loopback, Tailscale, an explicitly allowed network, or an authenticating reverse proxy (README.md:42-45, README.md:169-174).
- Uvicorn disables proxy-header trust, so direct client addresses—not untrusted X-Forwarded-For values—feed the network allowlist (app/api.py:735-737).
- Docker's default host publication is 127.0.0.1, although operators may deliberately set PUBLISH_ADDR=0.0.0.0 and broaden ALLOWED_NETS/ALLOWED_HOSTS (docker-compose.yml:18-30).
- The root policy resolver returned no SECURITY.md guidance; there is no supplied knowledge base or authoritative user threat model.
- It is not yet established whether all source metadata is operator-controlled or may be produced from less-trusted automated inputs, whether the optional reverse proxy rewrites schemes, or whether webhook/cookie features are enabled in a real deployment.
